problem: Security teams are overwhelmed by incident response work that could be automated with AI.
business_model: Enterprise security automation software (model not described in sources)

founders.name: Charles Whitby
founders.background_notes: YC page lists security certifications CISSP, PCIP, CRISC and CISM; no employers or education.

competitors.name: Demisto
competitors.what: Security orchestration, automation and response platform

technical_complexity.rationale: Automating incident response needs integrations with security tools and reliable AI decisions; the sources do not describe what was built.

defensibility.rationale: No evidence of data, integrations or customers; well funded SOAR vendors already existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: SOAR consolidated: Palo Alto Networks acquired Demisto in early 2019 and Splunk acquired Phantom, per a search summary of an SDxCentral article. Nothing shows these players reacting to Sublime Black.

market_need_then: Funded SOAR vendors in 2018 and 2019 show buyer spend on security automation. No evidence of demand specific to this company was found.

brand_strength.rationale: Only a YC page and a Built In listing mention the brand. It is easily confused with Sublime Security, a funded email security company.

outcome_analysis: Sublime Black is listed Inactive by YC with no description beyond a tagline, and no funding, press, shutdown notice or post-mortem was found. The cause of failure is not public, so no failure factors are asserted. Well funded SOAR competitors and quick consolidation in 2018 and 2019 formed the competitive backdrop.
notes: Website sublimeblack.com returned 404 (dead). Crunchbase snippet places the company in Rockville, Maryland and Built In lists Washington; unverified. Searches for funding returned only the unrelated Sublime Security. Swimlane source is dated June 2019, a few months after the Winter 2019 batch. Competitors listed are the named funded SOAR players, not proof of direct overlap.
